skill.name: observability-engineer
skill.description: Design production monitoring, logging, tracing, SLO, and incident response systems for reliable software operations.
skill.summary: Guides teams through observability strategy, telemetry design, alerting, SLOs, and incident response workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives from benign observability guidance. The skill describes monitoring design, access integration, and multi-cloud coverage, with no prompt injection or data exfiltration intent found. No semantic findings were added.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid logging sensitive data or secrets.
- Multi-cloud and hybrid monitoring strategies across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premises
- Active Directory and SAML integration for monitoring access

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 33 advises against logging sensitive data or secrets. This is protective guidance, not system reconnaissance or misuse.
Line 203 describes multi-cloud monitoring strategy knowledge. It does not instruct discovery, enumeration, or unauthorized access to cloud resources.
Line 164 references AD and SAML integration for monitoring access control. The context is enterprise identity integration, not network scanning or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Production systems fail without clear signals across metrics, logs, traces, and alerts. This skill designs observability strategies that improve reliability, incident response, and cost control.
actual_capabilities: Designs monitoring, logging, and tracing architectures for production services.
Defines SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and burn rate alerting strategies.
Recommends dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and escalation workflows for operations teams.
Plans OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Loki, and vendor observability integrations.
Reviews telemetry retention, sampling, cardinality, and cost optimization tradeoffs.
Connects reliability signals with compliance, security, and business impact reporting.
limitations: Requires accurate service, traffic, and telemetry context from the user.
Does not directly operate monitoring platforms or access live production systems.
Generated plans must be validated against real load, failure modes, and team processes.
Does not replace incident commander judgment during active production incidents.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Observability
use_cases.description: Design a consistent metrics, logging, tracing, and dashboard strategy for Kubernetes or cloud services.

use_cases.title: Build SLO-Based Operations
use_cases.description: Define SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, alert routing, and runbooks for customer-facing services.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Monitoring
use_cases.description: Map monitoring data, audit trails, access controls, and reporting needs for regulated environments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Monitoring Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monitoring plan for my service. Cover key metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerts, and the first runbooks.

prompt_templates.title: Define SLOs and Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Help define SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and burn rate alerts for this API using availability, latency, and error data.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Telemetry Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced team improving an existing stack.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our observability stack and recommend changes for OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, tracing, log retention, and alert noise.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Enterprise Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an enterprise observability migration plan across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premises systems with compliance and cost controls.

output_examples.input: Design monitoring for a checkout service with strict latency targets.
output_examples.output: A complete observability plan with SLIs, latency dashboards, trace requirements, alert thresholds, and incident runbooks.

output_examples.input: Reduce noisy alerts for a microservices platform.
output_examples.output: A prioritized alert review covering symptom-based alerts, burn rate rules, deduplication, escalation paths, and owner mapping.

output_examples.input: Plan OpenTelemetry adoption for several service teams.
output_examples.output: A phased rollout covering instrumentation standards, collector topology, sampling, backend exports, validation, and governance.

best_practices: Start with user journeys and reliability targets before choosing tools.
Use symptom-based alerts tied to SLO impact and clear ownership.
Review telemetry cost, retention, and cardinality during every design.
anti_patterns: Collecting every metric without a clear operational decision.
Alerting on low-level noise that does not affect users.
Logging sensitive data, tokens, or personal information in telemetry streams.

faq.question: Can this skill choose an observability stack?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare open source and commercial tools against scale, cost, retention, and team requirements.

faq.question: Does it support OpenTelemetry planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers instrumentation, collectors, exporters, sampling, standards, and phased adoption plans.

faq.question: Can it help during an incident?
faq.answer: It can structure investigation steps, signal review, escalation, and follow-up actions. It should not replace live incident leadership.

faq.question: Will it write dashboard or alert definitions?
faq.answer: It can draft dashboard layouts and alert logic. Teams should test every rule against real production data.

faq.question: Is this only for large enterprises?
faq.answer: No. It can scale recommendations from startup systems to multi-cloud enterprise environments.

faq.question: How should I prepare a request?
faq.answer: Provide service goals, traffic patterns, current tools, known incidents, compliance needs, and cost constraints.
